law_record.title: Rail crossings at grade
law_record.text: The prima facie speed limit shall be fifteen miles per hour when traversing a grade crossing of a steam, electric or any other motor railway, if during the last one hundred feet of the approach to such crossing the driver does not have a clear and unobstructed view of such crossing and of any traffic on such railway for a distance of four hundred feet in both directions along such railway. This Section shall not apply in the case of any railway grade crossing where a human flagman is on duty or clearly visible electrical or mechanical railway crossing signal device is installed but does not then indicate the immediate approach of a railway train or car.

activation_conditions: the subject traverses a railway grade crossing
during the last 100 feet of the approach the driver lacks a clear view of the crossing and of railway traffic 400 feet in both directions
exceptions: where a human flagman is on duty
where a clearly visible electrical or mechanical crossing signal is installed and is not then indicating the immediate approach of a train
residue: 'prima facie' means the limit is rebuttable in law; a monitor can only report the speed against it
the view of the crossing itself is the region's sight distance; the traffic on the railway within 400 feet is read through rel.visible, which the source must supply
summary.subject: driver

timing_requirements.requirement: the limit binds through the approach and the traversal
the sight condition is evaluated over the last 100 feet before the crossing, so the speed must already be down on entering that stretch
